text:
Jonathan Marchessault has been out since Nov 1, listed day-to-day, and Nashville won four straight without him. That's the uncomfortable context for a player who signed in Nashville as a Conn Smythe winner and has struggled to look like one.

The numbers this season are rough. The Predators have only 33% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 18 points worse than without him. All five of his points have come on the power play. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents creating much more with him on the ice (bottom 3% of forwards).

There's still a power-play shooter in there, and he's shooting 6.5% against a normal range around 11%, so some goals are coming whenever he's back. He's 35, undrafted, with a Cup and a playoff MVP from Vegas in 2023. Our projection sees about 18 goals if he plays every game. The question for Nashville is where he fits in a lineup that's winning without him.
